chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There burst into the Euphrates every day bursts from Paradise.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: jannah — Paradise, the Garden; the eternal abode of the righteous
key_terms.الْفُرَاتِ: the Euphrates — one of the four great rivers mentioned as flowing from Paradise in some traditions
key_terms.دُفُقَاتٌ: plural of dufuqah — a burst, a gush, a surge of water
key_terms.يُدْفَقُ: from dafaqa — to pour, to gush, to surge; used for rushing water

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Euphrates river and Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that the Euphrates river receives daily infusions of water from Paradise itself. This narration reflects the Islamic cosmological understanding that the physical world maintains sacred connections to the divine realm, and that certain rivers and places carry a celestial blessing. The Euphrates (al-Furat), one of the great rivers of the ancient world flowing through Iraq, was particularly revered in Islamic tradition as a blessed river.
